segments.speaker: assembly-of-gods-1
segments.caption: The gods take their places in a widening ring. Poseidon’s seat remains empty.
segments.delivery: listening immortals whose collective attention moves from Zeus to Athena

segments.speaker: zeus
segments.caption: Zeus
segments.delivery: troubled sovereign speaking from seated authority, then defending the gods' treatment of Odysseus

segments.speaker: zeus
segments.caption: How mortals love to blame the gods for their sorrows. Think of Aegisthus, who took Agamemnon's wife and cut the king down at his homecoming, though we sent Hermes himself to warn him. His own recklessness doubled the fate he was owed.
segments.delivery: troubled sovereign speaking from seated authority, then defending the gods' treatment of Odysseus

segments.speaker: athena
segments.caption: Athena
segments.delivery: bright-eyed strategist shifting the assembly from abstract blame to a concrete rescue plan

segments.speaker: athena
segments.caption: Father Zeus, let Aegisthus lie in the ruin he earned. It is Odysseus my heart breaks for, wise, unlucky Odysseus, held against his will on Calypso's island, longing only for the sight of smoke rising from his own hearth. Has he not paid you sacrifice enough on the plain of Troy, Olympian?
segments.delivery: bright-eyed strategist shifting the assembly from abstract blame to a concrete rescue plan

segments.speaker: zeus
segments.caption: My child, how could I forget godlike Odysseus? It is Poseidon the earth-shaker who rages without rest for the blinding of his Cyclops son, and drives that man from his homecoming. But come, let us here shape his return; one god cannot hold out against us all.
segments.delivery: troubled sovereign speaking from seated authority, then defending the gods' treatment of Odysseus

beat.note: she is petitioning Zeus, not commanding him
